mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.0% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its previous 12-month maximum for three consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO exceeds 12-month maximum for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month maximum for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index above their previous 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous 12-month average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its previous 12-month maximum for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 12-month maximum for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month maximum for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its previous 12-month minimum for four consecutive months signals a consumption-led demand surge, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 12-month minimum for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS is below its 12-month minimum for four consecutive months.
